labels.label: bzthm:c2s2_proprietes_pseudo_longueur
labels.notes: Read against benzecri1960_ch2.tex l.229-258 and the scan (PDF p. 22 = journal p. 249). The transcription matches the scan, and so does the docstring's > quote. Definitions underneath, checked: pseudoLength (Mesure.lean:299) is the EReal infimum of the k with IsMajoreSeg, which is Def. 2 and is top off segments. IsProjSegment (Classes.lean:168) is Def. 14; its segments are compact, being the image of closedSeg under the chart inverse. hilbertLength K A B (Hilbert.lean:1056) is by definition the pseudoLength of the unique segment of corpsInterior K. GXAut is Def. 15. IsPocheProj (Poches.lean:585) is Def. 1'. CONJUNCT BY CONJUNCT, Lean >= paper. 1 deg: nonnegativity holds for every (Sg, M, N), a segment or not, and l(M, M) = 0 holds for every segment from M to M (weaker hypotheses). 2 deg: for every g in GXAut (GSR n) (S n) V, the image segment g(Sg) keeps its length, with no segment hypothesis. The reading of l_V(gM, gN) as the image segment is the only one in which both sides are the same segment. 3 deg: only (Sg, M, N) must be a segment; Sg' is arbitrary (top off segments), which is weaker than both being segments. 4 deg: W : Opens V with Mathlib's induced charts, any Sg in W with no segment hypothesis. 5 deg: two forms. (i) The neighbourhood form: for every k > l(Sg) there are an open U containing Sg and a neighbourhood of (M, N) such that every segment inside U with endpoints there has l < k. This is upper semicontinuity in the coarsest topology on (segment, endpoints) that has the upper Vietoris sets. (ii) A limsup along any filter on any index type, sequences included: the endpoints converge, and the segments are eventually inside every open U containing Sg. ON THE CALLER'S QUESTION: this convergence hypothesis is WEAKER than every standard notion of convergence of segments, so the theorem is stronger. Segments are compact and the paper's V is metrizable, so Hausdorff convergence of the segments implies 'eventually inside U' (with the endpoints, as the paper's (M_i, N_i) -> (M, N) writes them); so do Vietoris convergence, uniform convergence of parametrisations, and convergence in one chart around Sg. The printed proof of 5 deg (l.322-330) uses exactly this: 'tout segment assez voisin de MN' must lie in the chart neighbourhood U of (A, B). The only plausible weaker reading, endpoints alone, makes 5 deg false, so no faithful statement could certify it. The closer's conclusion on that point is correct, but its counterexample is wrong (major finding below). The mark is therefore legitimate for 5 deg: the formal statement implies the paper's under every reading in which the paper is true, and the residual question stays an OQ. 6 deg: read literally, V = corpsInterior K for IsCorpsConvexeS n K. It states uniqueness and existence of the segment (so l_V is a function of (M, N)), l_V = hilbertLength K, continuity into EReal and into R, finiteness, and l_V(M, N) = 0 iff M = N. The literal reading is the paper's own: the printed proof of 6 deg is 'resulte de la proposition 2' (l.303), and Prop. 2 is literally the interior of a convex body. The up-to-isomorphism use belongs to the proof of Prop. 3 (l.373-376) and is disclosed in the questions. 7 deg: IsPocheProj with (exists y, z y /= 0) is DEC-178's 'z non-constant', proved equivalent for a pocket (IsPocheProj.exists_ne_zero_iff_nonconstant; also equivalent to 'non-constant on phi(P)', because an affine form constant on a nonempty open set is constant). Dropping K > 1 is a pure generalisation: for K <= 0, z(phi M) >= 0 contradicts z(phi M) < 1/K; for 0 < K <= 1, l >= 0 contradicts l < log K <= 0. Dropping the segment hypothesis is also a generalisation, since l < log K < top forces a segment. The conclusion is N in P and z(phi N) < K z(phi M). Dimension: [NeZero n] under DEC-177. V carries only ChartedSpace and HasGroupoid; T2, connected and second countable are dropped, which is a weakening. MARK: **`bzthm:c2s2_proprietes_pseudo_longueur`** - `benzecri1960_ch2.tex:229` sits at line 11, within the first 4000 characters. It marks the corrected form only under DEC-206 (one statement), DEC-177 (n >= 1) and DEC-178 (z non-constant), the rows the dispatch names. Status 'closed' with a findings entry is consistent: that entry consolidates OQ-45 and OQ-61, both already ruled. PRINTED REFUTATION: ProprietesPseudoLongueurPrinted is no stronger than the printed text in the two conjuncts the refutation uses: 1 deg with the segment hypothesis, and 7 deg with K > 1, a segment, and IsPocheProj as printed, over T2, connected, second-countable V : Type. So not_proprietesPseudoLongueurPrinted is a valid refutation of the printed enonce, as ruled in OQ-45 and OQ-61. NON-VACUITY: exists_isPocheProj_cote_ne_zero (n = 1) and exists_ne_corpsInterior_iff (Prop2Literal.lean:293) exist. The constant family makes the 5 deg hypotheses satisfiable.

findings.where: REPORT.json labels[0].questions[0] (the flat-annulus argument for 5 deg); echoed without numbers in Proprietes.lean:101-103
findings.what: The counterexample offered to the author is false as stated. The REPORT takes V = (R/Z) x ]0,1[, M = [0, 0.45], N = [0.6, 0.55], and claims that 'a segment of V containing sigma lies on its line and has x-span < 1 (injectivity)', so that l_V(sigma_1) = log 16 and l_V(sigma_2) = log(49/9). These segments are not horizontal (slopes 1/6 and -1/4). On a non-horizontal line no two points differ by (m, 0), so its projection to the annulus is injective, and a thin tube around it embeds, whatever its x-span. A segment containing sigma_1 can then run along its line across the whole strip, from y = eps to y = 1 - eps (x-span about 6), and it is a segment of V: the chart is the developing map on the embedded tube. The affine parameter on that line is proportional to y, so for both sigma_1 and sigma_2 the pseudo-length is log((0.55 * 0.55)/(0.45 * 0.45)) = log(121/81), about 0.40. The two segments have the SAME pseudo-length, and the example refutes nothing. The conclusion it was meant to support is nevertheless true: endpoint convergence alone does not make 5 deg hold. The sentence 'its limsup log 16 exceeds l_V(sigma_2)' would reach the author as a fact, and it is false.
findings.fix: In REPORT.json questions[0], make the segments horizontal: M = [0, 1/2], N = [3/5, 1/2], with sigma_1 of x-span 3/5 and sigma_2 of x-span 2/5. A segment of V containing a horizontal sigma lies on the closed horizontal geodesic y = 1/2, and injectivity on the segment does force x-span L < 1 there. The infimum over L -> 1, placed symmetrically, gives l_V = log((1+d)/(1-d))^2: log 16 for sigma_1 and log(49/9) for sigma_2, so the constant family sigma_1 refutes the endpoints-only reading. Alternatively, state only the conclusion and drop the numbers. The Lean file needs no change: its SCOPE says only 'a flat annulus', which stays true. Re-audit is a check of the REPORT text only.

issues.problem: The flat-annulus counterexample for the endpoints-only reading of 5 deg is wrong as stated. M = [0, 0.45] and N = [0.6, 0.55] give non-horizontal segments, which are not limited to x-span < 1. Both segments have pseudo-length log(121/81), so the claimed log 16 > log(49/9) is false. The conclusion (endpoint convergence alone is not enough) is true.
issues.fix: Use horizontal segments M = [0, 1/2], N = [3/5, 1/2], for which l_V = log 16 and log(49/9) do hold; or drop the numbers.

notes: Answer to the dispatch's question on 5 deg: the Lean convergence hypothesis (endpoints converge, and the segments are eventually inside every open set containing the limit segment) is WEAKER than each standard notion: Hausdorff or Vietoris convergence with the endpoints, uniform convergence of parametrisations, and convergence in one chart around Sg. The Lean theorem is therefore STRONGER than the paper's 5 deg under each of them, not narrower, and the neighbourhood form adds upper semicontinuity in the coarsest such topology. Under the endpoints-only reading the paper's 5 deg is false (corrected example in the finding), so no faithful certificate exists for that reading; it stays a question to the author. Not a finding: 6 deg is read literally, which is the paper's own reading, since its printed proof is Prop. 2. The isomorphism-invariant form that the proof of Prop. 3 applies through a chart would need l_V to be invariant under projective isomorphisms between two manifolds, which is a 2 deg-type transport lemma worth having for Prop. 3's row. Once the REPORT text is corrected, the file is ready to graduate with the mark as proposed.
